desk_read: Yesterday's session was defined by an energy rally driven by new longs while metals and equities faced selling pressure. In WTI Crude Oil and Brent NYMEX, prices rose +2.55% and +3.11% alongside total open interest increases of +6.8k contracts (+0.5%) and +4.4k contracts (+3.4%), maintaining backwardation. Natural Gas also saw new longs with price up +3.89% and total open interest up +4.0k contracts (+0.3%) on volume of 1.5x its 20-day average. Conversely, Silver suffered a -3.72% price drop while total open interest surged +6.6k contracts (+5.7%) on volume of 1.1x its 20-day average, signaling new shorts. In equities, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 experienced long liquidation with total open interest dropping -3.8k contracts (-0.2%) and -3.7k contracts (-1.3%).
oil_read: WTI crude oil (most active CLZ26) rallied +2.55% with total open interest up +6.8k contracts (+0.5%) on 0.8x average volume, reading as new longs into a backwardated curve where the CLZ26-CLK27 spread widened +6.46 $/bbl. Brent NYMEX (most active BZG27) gained +3.11% as total open interest rose +4.4k contracts (+3.4%) on 0.6x average volume, signaling new longs within backwardation with the BZF27-BZM27 spread at +9.21 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil displays a bullish bias with fresh long positions and a steepening backwardation, while Brent shows a mildly bullish bias with new longs on light volume 0.6x the 20-day average, meaning this positioning supports the current trend. Natural Gas exhibits a mildly bullish bias with new longs and a volume 1.5x the 20-day average, showing strong conviction that supports the move higher. Conversely, Copper displays a mildly bearish bias with new shorts, which warns of downward pressure. Overall, the flow reveals divergence across asset classes, with energy positioning supporting upside continuation while metals and equities reflect cautious sentiment.
